note: Written for Which AI Map. Words in [brackets] are what you fill in. They work in Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot unless a tool is named.

prompts.title: Reply to a difficult email
prompts.text:
Here is an email I received:

[paste the email]

Write a reply that is calm and polite but firm. My position: [what you want to say]. Keep it under 150 words. Give me two versions: one warmer, one more formal.
prompts.tip: Paste the whole thread if there were earlier messages: tone depends on history.

prompts.title: Make my text clearer
prompts.text:
Rewrite the text below so it is clearer and shorter, without changing what it says or adding anything new. Keep my voice. Then list the three biggest changes you made and why.

[paste your text]
prompts.tip: Asking for the list of changes lets you undo the ones you disagree with.

prompts.title: Proofread without rewriting
prompts.text:
Proofread this text. Only fix spelling, grammar and punctuation; do not change wording or style. Show each correction as: original → corrected.

[paste your text]
prompts.tip: Good for texts in a second language when you want to stay sounding like yourself.

prompts.title: A LinkedIn post from my notes
prompts.text:
Turn these notes into a LinkedIn post of about 150 words. Audience: [who]. Start with one concrete sentence, not a question. No hashtags in the text, no emoji, no clichés like 'game-changer'. End with a simple question to invite comments.

Notes: [your notes]
prompts.tip: Say what you want to avoid: models default to a very 'LinkedIn' style otherwise.

prompts.title: Translate so it sounds natural
prompts.text:
Translate this into [language] for [who will read it]. Make it sound like it was written by a native speaker, not translated. Keep names, numbers and technical terms exactly as they are. Point out any phrase that has no good equivalent.

[paste the text]
prompts.tip: For long documents with layout, DeepL keeps the formatting better.

prompts.title: Summarize a long document
prompts.text: Summarize the attached document for someone who has 2 minutes. Give: (1) the main point in one sentence, (2) the five most important facts with page or section numbers, (3) anything that needs a decision or action, with deadlines.
prompts.tip: Asking for page numbers makes it easy to check the summary against the source.

prompts.title: Find the catch in a contract
prompts.text:
Read this contract as if you were advising me, the [tenant / buyer / freelancer]. List: what I am committing to, every cost or fee, how I can end it and what that costs, and any clause that is unusual or one-sided. Quote the exact clause for each point. Then list questions I should ask before signing.

[attach or paste the contract]
prompts.tip: It helps you prepare questions; it does not replace a lawyer for anything important.

prompts.title: Explain an official letter
prompts.text:
I received this letter from [the tax office / my bank / a utility]. Explain in plain words what it says, what they want from me, by when, and what happens if I do nothing.

[paste the letter, remove your ID numbers first]
prompts.tip: Remove account numbers, ID numbers and your address before pasting.

prompts.title: Turn a transcript into meeting notes
prompts.text:
Here is a meeting transcript. Write meeting notes with: decisions made, action items as a table (task, owner, deadline), open questions, and a three-sentence summary for people who missed it. Do not include anything that was not said.

[paste the transcript]
prompts.tip: Otter, Fireflies or Granola can record the transcript for you.

prompts.title: Explain a topic from zero
prompts.text: Explain [topic] to me as if I am smart but new to it. Start with a one-paragraph overview, then the five ideas I must understand, each with an everyday example. Finish with three questions I can answer to check that I understood.
prompts.tip: Answer the three questions in the chat and ask it to correct you.

prompts.title: A study plan with a deadline
prompts.text: I want to learn [skill] well enough to [goal] by [date]. I can spend [hours] per week. Make a week-by-week plan with what to learn, one free resource for each week and a small exercise to prove I learned it.
prompts.tip: Ask for free resources only, or it may suggest paid courses.

prompts.title: Quiz me before an exam
prompts.text:
Quiz me on [subject], using the notes below. Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer. After each answer tell me if it was right, explain briefly, and make the next question harder if I was right or easier if I was wrong.

[paste your notes]
prompts.tip: NotebookLM does this well when your course material is uploaded there.

prompts.title: Check my understanding
prompts.text: Here is my explanation of [topic]: [your explanation]. Point out anything that is wrong or missing, and what a teacher would mark down. Be direct.
prompts.tip: Explaining something back is one of the fastest ways to learn it.

prompts.title: Write a job advert
prompts.text: Write a job advert for a [role] at [company: one line about it]. Must-haves: [list]. Nice to have: [list]. Salary range: [range]. Tone: friendly and specific, no buzzwords. Under 300 words, with a clear 'how to apply' at the end.
prompts.tip: Including the salary range gets more relevant applicants.

prompts.title: Answer an unhappy customer
prompts.text: A customer wrote this complaint: [paste it]. The facts: [what happened]. What we can offer: [refund / replacement / discount]. Write a reply that apologizes for what went wrong without admitting more than the facts, explains what we will do, and keeps them as a customer. Under 120 words.
prompts.tip: Give it the facts; otherwise it may promise things you cannot do.

prompts.title: Tough feedback on my idea
prompts.text: Here is my business idea: [describe it]. Act as a sceptical investor. Give me the five strongest reasons it could fail, the questions you would ask in a meeting, and what evidence would change your mind. Do not be encouraging.
prompts.tip: AI tends to praise ideas; asking for scepticism gives a more useful answer.

prompts.title: Outline for a presentation
prompts.text: Make an outline for a [10]-minute presentation about [topic] for [audience]. For each slide: a title that states the point, three bullet points, and what to show (chart, photo or nothing). End with one slide that says what I want the audience to do.
prompts.tip: Paste the outline into Gamma to turn it into finished slides.

prompts.title: A status update for my manager
prompts.text:
Turn these notes into a short status update for my manager: done this week, in progress, blocked (and what I need to unblock it), next week. Five lines per section at most.

Notes: [your notes]

prompts.title: Compare options fairly
prompts.text: Help me choose between [option A], [option B] and [option C]. What matters to me, in order: [list]. Make a table that scores each option on each point, explain the scores, and tell me which you would pick and what would make you change your mind.
prompts.tip: For prices and recent facts, use an assistant with web search and open its sources.

prompts.title: Plan a trip
prompts.text: Plan [number] days in [place] for [who is going] in [month]. Budget: [amount]. We like [interests] and dislike [dislikes]. Give a day-by-day plan with a morning, afternoon and evening, travel time between places, and one rainy-day alternative per day.
prompts.tip: Check opening hours and prices yourself: they are often out of date.

prompts.title: Imagine it went wrong
prompts.text: I am about to [decision]. Imagine it is a year from now and it turned out badly. Write the most likely story of what went wrong, then list what I can do now to prevent each part of that story.
prompts.tip: This 'pre-mortem' finds risks that a pros and cons list misses.

prompts.title: Plan my week
prompts.text: Here are my tasks for the week with rough time estimates: [list]. Fixed appointments: [list]. I work best on hard tasks in the [morning / afternoon]. Make a realistic day-by-day plan with breaks, and tell me what to drop if the week fills up.

prompts.title: Write a prompt for an image tool
prompts.text: I want an image of [idea] for [where it will be used]. Write three different prompts I can paste into an image generator: one photographic, one illustration, one minimal. Each should describe subject, setting, light, colours and composition in one paragraph.
prompts.tip: Use the result in Midjourney, Ideogram (good with text in images) or ChatGPT's image tool.

prompts.title: Logo ideas for a small business
prompts.text: My business: [name], [what it does], for [customers]. Feel: [three words]. Suggest five logo concepts, each with the idea behind it, the shape, two colours with hex codes and a font style. Then write an image prompt for the strongest one.
prompts.tip: Ideogram is the best of the image tools at spelling the name correctly.

prompts.title: A bedtime story
prompts.text: Write a five-minute bedtime story for a [age]-year-old who loves [things]. The hero is called [name]. Include a small problem that is solved by being kind or brave, gentle humour, and a calm ending. Simple words.

prompts.title: Lyrics for a song
prompts.text: Write song lyrics for [occasion] about [person or story]. Style: [genre]. Two verses, a chorus that repeats, and a short bridge. Include these details: [names, inside jokes].
prompts.tip: Paste the lyrics into Suno to turn them into a finished song.

prompts.title: Write a spreadsheet formula
prompts.text: I use [Excel / Google Sheets]. Column A has [what], column B has [what]. I want column C to show [result]. Write the formula for C2, explain each part, and tell me what happens if a cell is empty.
prompts.tip: Describe the columns precisely; that matters more than the wording.

prompts.title: Explain an error message
prompts.text:
I got this error when [what you were doing]:

[paste the error]

Explain in plain words what it means, the most likely cause, and the steps to fix it, starting with the easiest. I am not a programmer.
prompts.tip: Paste the full error text, not a description of it.

prompts.title: A small automation script
prompts.text: Write a script that [task, e.g. renames all photos in a folder by the date they were taken]. I use [Windows / Mac]. Explain how to run it step by step, and make it ask for confirmation before changing any files.
prompts.tip: Try it on a copy of your files first.

prompts.title: Review my code
prompts.text:
Review this code for bugs, security problems and unclear parts. List problems from most to least serious, with the line and a fix for each. Do not rewrite everything.

[paste the code]
prompts.tip: Claude Code or Cursor can do this across a whole project.

prompts.title: A week of meals and the shopping list
prompts.text: Plan dinners for [number] people for 5 days. Budget around [amount]. Rules: [diet, allergies, dislikes]. Max [minutes] of cooking a day. Give the meals, then one combined shopping list grouped by supermarket section.

prompts.title: A workout plan I can keep
prompts.text: Make a [number]-week workout plan for a [beginner / intermediate], [age], with [equipment or none]. Goal: [goal]. [number] sessions a week, max [minutes] each. Explain how to know if a session is too easy or too hard.
prompts.tip: Check with a doctor first if you have health conditions.

prompts.title: Make sense of my spending
prompts.text: Here are my monthly spending categories and amounts: [list]. My income is [amount]. Show where the money goes as percentages, compare with a common guideline such as 50/30/20, and suggest three realistic changes with how much each would save.
prompts.tip: Use categories and totals, not your bank statement: never paste account numbers.

prompts.title: Gift ideas that are not generic
prompts.text: Suggest ten gift ideas for [person: age, relationship] who likes [interests] and already has [things]. Budget: [amount]. Mix things, experiences and something handmade. Skip anything generic like mugs or socks.

prompts.title: Prepare a hard conversation
prompts.text: I need to talk to [person] about [issue]. What I want: [outcome]. What I am worried about: [worry]. Help me plan: how to open the conversation, what to say if they get defensive, and how to end it whatever happens. Then let me practise: you play them and react realistically.
prompts.tip: The practice round at the end is the most useful part.
